About.Name: Jake R Graham
About.AboutText: My name is Jake Graham; I am a dedicated and hard-working Computer Engineering student at Seattle Pacific University.

Experience.ExperienceText: Beyond my education, I serve in a minor role on my church's tech team, where I alternately run the lights or the broadcast audio for the service. I also routinely perform repairs on my house, its appliances, and my car, including changing batteries and caliper pins on my car, installing new power outlets, changing batteries on laptops, and other such necessities.
Experience.EducationText: I have an aptitude for mathematics, computer science, and engineering. Because of these, I was highly encouraged throughout my life to pursue an engineering degree. I initially resisted the idea when I graduated from High School because I didn't particularly enjoy either the experience or the classes, but after taking a year off I was encouraged to continue my education, and to my delight, I found that all of the interesting classes I had been wanting were found in Higher Education. Since that discovery, I have been working and studying hard to get a Computer Engineering degree in order to become an Embedded Engineer, where I hope to use my math, computer science, and engineering skills to create new solutions for complex problems.

Project1.Title: GPU exploration
Project1.Desc: I was an intern at a company called Symetrix, who makes audio equipment, in the summer of 2026. During that internship, I learned how GPUs work, I learned a language called SYCL which is designed to target multiple processing units at once, and I gained first-hand experience with programming in a real-time backend environment. The goal of my internship was twofold: to figure out how to run code on a GPU, and then make an API that would allow developers to make the call of whether or not the GPU was worth using for any use that may come to mind in the future.
